title: Hospital Equipment Purchase
description: Your hospital committee must recommend one MRI system for a major equipment purchase that will affect patient throughput, diagnostic reliability, staff workload, and service planning. Three vendors remain under consideration after the initial procurement review. Examine the evidence carefully and recommend the best option for the hospital.
p1_persona: You are a clinical quality representative on the hospital equipment committee. Your focus is patient safety, diagnostic coverage, workflow fit for clinicians, and whether the system supports reliable care.
p2_persona: You are a procurement and service planning representative on the hospital equipment committee. Your focus is vendor reliability, maintenance risk, long-term support, and operational continuity.
correct_rationale: Pooled: A has fatal flaws (P2: recalls, service collapse, lowest accuracy). B has fatal flaws (P1: 3T safety incident, FDA inspection, can't cover 35% of caseload). C has only mild logistical drawbacks. C wins by elimination.
shared_info: The MediScan Pro 5000 has the fastest scan time at 8 minutes per session
The NeuroVision Elite specialises in neurological imaging with 3T magnet strength
The OmniImage 360 is a general-purpose system with 1.5T magnet strength and is the newest of the three product lines
p1_unique_info: The NeuroVision Elite's 3T magnet caused a serious adverse event involving an implanted device at a peer hospital last year, prompting an internal safety review
The NeuroVision Elite's manufacturer is currently under FDA inspection for quality-assurance process violations following a whistleblower complaint
The NeuroVision Elite's neurological specialisation means 35% of the hospital's musculoskeletal MRI referrals would need to be sent out, at an estimated $400K/year in outsourcing costs
The OmniImage 360's 1.5T strength means very fine neurological imaging requires longer scan times (~12 min vs ~8 min for higher-strength systems)
The OmniImage 360 is manufactured overseas, so spare parts have a 2-week lead time vs same-week for the other two
The OmniImage 360's larger footprint would require minor renovation work in Bay 3 before installation
p2_unique_info: The MediScan Pro 5000 has been recalled twice in 3 years for software glitches that produced false-negative scans, and a third recall is rumoured to be under FDA review
The MediScan Pro 5000's manufacturer was recently acquired by a private-equity firm and is cutting its US technician workforce by 40% over 18 months — service response times are projected to triple
In a head-to-head clinical trial, the MediScan Pro 5000 had only 91% diagnostic accuracy across all imaging types, the lowest of the three systems
The OmniImage 360's interface received a 3.1/5 usability rating from radiology technologists in a 2025 survey (vs ~4.0 for the others)
The OmniImage 360 is a younger product line (released 2023), so long-term reliability data is thinner than the established competitors
The OmniImage 360's vendor has a smaller US service network — only 3 regional service hubs
anchor_rationale: The MediScan Pro 5000 has the fastest scan time, which seems most efficient
